release.note: The owner's release rules (RUBRIC §3, §4, §8 and §10). Two candidates in a row were held for a day by the pre-deploy deep review although each was better than the live build; Bailey was offered three answers and replied "A, B, and C together please." (2026-09-21). A: a build ships when its reviewed changed area has no critical defect introduced or left reachable by the change and no regression against the live build; majors that are not regressions are disclosed and carried into the next batch; a defect inside a brand-new feature does not block (the feature may ship switched off). B: a shared-system change needs a FOCUSED review of the production candidate before the deploy and its DEEP review after it, on the live build. C: the owner override (2026-09-21, commit d333b06) is unchanged.
release.requiredFromNote: Reports dated on or after this day must carry verdicts.ship, shipReasons and the two tags on every critical or major issue. Rounds 04 to 06 predate the rule and stay valid as history.
release.deepBeforeDeployNote: Only the save-data class (src/app/SaveData.ts, save schema or migration, anything that can lose a player's progress) still needs deep evidence BEFORE the deploy. A milestone claim keeps it too, because the milestone standard did not change.

continuity.note: CHK-026 (size continuity across pose changes) and CHK-027 (continuity of motion), measured by critic/runner/lib/continuity.mjs (Bailey, 2026-10-04: D-420 to D-426). The thresholds the owner named are the first four numbers of `size`; every other number is derived and the reasoning is in docs/handoff/critic-continuity.md and critic/CHECKS.md. tools/critic-policy.mjs reads `caps` and `requiredFrom`; the harness reads the rest.
continuity.requiredFromNote: A deep or milestone report dated on or after this day that carries subScores must record CHK-026 and CHK-027 (any result, UNVERIFIED needs its reason), and its characterModels and animation sub-scores obey `caps`. Reports before it (rounds 19 to 21 carry subScores) stay valid as history.

readings.note: Pose continuity W4 (docs/plans/pose-continuity-review.md section 5; the release driver's decision 6 of 2026-10-16, under Bailey 2026-10-16: "pose continuity is the strongest recurring issue we need a permanent fix for this please." and, on Lulu's hurt, "lulu looks tiny when hurt - this problem again? ugh"). CHK-026 read the head from the registration table the engine itself draws with, so it passed any registered pose by construction (Lulu's hurt was drawn at 0.667 of her idle's height for ten releases with CHK-026 green). Three readings from the pixels, taken from a swap's two planes in the same frame: HEIGHT (a pose drawn against the idle, stature; length for a KO, report-only; bands from tools/posescale/pose-bands.mjs, the gate's own), FEET (the silhouette's own stance, whatever stance the registration claims: the vertical gap when both stances are registered, both axes when one is not) and the REAL HEAD across a recorded hold (the registered head box is virtual there). The head reading stays and is labelled control. A pose in docs/target/pose-waivers.json is read and shown, never failed. false switches one reading off, for an old-versus-new run of one recording.

jerks.note: Pose continuity W4, CHK-027 split (the release driver's decision 6 of 2026-10-16, under Bailey 2026-10-16: "pose continuity is the strongest recurring issue we need a permanent fix for this please."): a jerk AT a pose swap (a dissolve moving the weighted point, a KO cut) is gateable; a MID-MOVE dash (a lunge, a recoil, a hop) is the move's own and is reported, with the frame time each fell on, not gated. Bailey has not ruled on gating dashes separately (plan section 5 lists it under 'his to rule on'): this is the driver's split, in force until he says otherwise. true gates the dashes as every jerk was gated before; a policy without this block gates every jerk. teleportPx (300 px at 1600 wide) is the one safety the split adds: no lunge covers its whole reach in one frame (the longest, 2.23 units, is about 330 px, and its first frame is 19 to 40 percent of it, angle 2 section 4.2; the worst dash in the six r50.1 recordings is 136 px), so a mid-move step of 300 px or more is a TELEPORT (Anima's head 900 px under the Save Sphere's wash is the case on record) and is gated like a swap's; 0 gives the plain split back.

waivers.note: The gate's ledger (tools/pose-gate.mjs; CONTRACT-CHANGES 2026-10-16): one row per (subject, pose, painting sha). The harness shows a waived pose and does not fail it, so a live review and a deploy refusal cannot disagree about which poses may be off. A row whose sha names another painting than the record's is stale and is not honoured (Bailey 2026-10-16, the permanent fix: a re-installed painting loses its waiver). false judges every pose.

tracking.note: r40 instrument edit (a), Bailey 2026-10-10 (P5): a figure none of whose paintings has a registered head or stance is followed frame to frame by its silhouette's centroid, not by the middle of the lowest thick part. 'feet' gives the earlier reading back (for an old-versus-new run on the same recording). W4 (probe version 2, Bailey 2026-10-16, the permanent fix for pose continuity): `camera: 'point'` subtracts the camera's shift of each TRACKED point (a head 1.8 units above the origin is moved by far more than the origin is; the origin-only subtraction read a camera cut as a 40 to 57 px head jerk on every figure in the frame, angle 2 section 4.7), 'origin' gives the earlier reading back; a recording from probe version 1 has no per-point shift and always uses the origin's.

staged.note: r40 instrument edit (b), Bailey 2026-10-10 (P4, P5): a swap with a twirl-* key on either side is one staged costume change, not a snap; steps of one figure that continue from each other within gapFrames are one change. false gives the earlier reading back.

wash.note: r43 instrument edit (docs/handoff/r41-aeonjump.md, FOC40-02), FFX-2 only in effect (only Chapter XI plays a Save Sphere card). The excuse ships OFF until the owner says yes: the definition of a jerk is Bailey's (D-420 to D-426), r41-aeonjump listed it as an option 'neither built (rule 10: ideas need a yes)', and no yes of his is recorded. Off, every jerk is counted as before; the probe still records the opacity of the card's wash on every frame it is up, and a jerk whose step (frame n-1 to n) was under it carries the wash over it in continuity.json (evidence only). On, a jerk whose step was under a wash that hides at least minCover of the picture (opacity x background alpha; the veil tops out at 0.74, so about 26 percent of the picture still shows through it) is tagged covered and left out of the summary, the verdict and the worst-jerk strips. The case is Anima's head step in Chapter XI (960 px in one frame in r41-aeonjump's trace, 967.7 px in round 25's dedicated run), which happens under the wash: the run's headline worst jerk, but not what decides the chapter (round 25 has 15 more jerks of 40 px or more there). To turn it on: quote his words and date in this note (tests/unit/critic-continuity-policy.test.ts asks for it), add the D-row, and use the minCover he picks (0.7: the wash essentially all the way up; 0.5 also excuses a half-faded veil). CONT_CFG='{"wash":{"excuse":true}}' runs the what-if for one run; selector null stops the probe reading the wash.

intentionalFlatImagesNote: Shipped images that are deliberately one flat colour (2026-10-03, release 37; the .webp spellings added in release 38, where a build ships the same layers as lossless WebP derived from these PNG masters, tools/art-derive-lib.mjs). Paine's right-eye catchlight layers are fully transparent: the source painting has no catchlight on that eye, so tools/portrait-parts.py copies an empty layer, and src/app/screens/pause/livingRender.ts draws it over nothing (no error, no visible change). Harmless; disclosed. An alpha MASK (one RGB value with an alpha shape, e.g. the eye windows) is not flat and needs no entry: tools/artifact-manifest.mjs counts alpha.

alwaysAtDeployStatic.title: Static pose census: every shipped character painting read against its idle (class, stature, real head, feet, overlap, status, waiver), no browser
alwaysAtDeployStatic.note: Pose continuity W4 (docs/plans/pose-continuity-review.md section 5; Bailey 2026-10-16: the permanent fix). Every candidate gets it, whatever the plan says (a live-only candidate included), because a pose can be out of band without a changed file: the waiver ledger is a record, not a build. It is data for the report, not a verdict: the gate itself (tools/pose-gate.mjs --check) refuses at install and at deploy. A reviewer runs each command of this list from the candidate's root ({evidence} is the review's evidence folder), copies the file's `totals` into the report as `staticChecks.pose-census`, and says so when public/art is absent (the check is then UNVERIFIED for this candidate, never PASS). It is not CHK-026 itself: CHK-026 stays the browser harness's, with its own schedule, so listing it here adds no check to the plan.

baseline.note: Evidence baseline for dependency reuse under policy v2. Its A/B/C numbers are historical (rubric v1) and are never shown as a v2 score.

Advice stays useful on damaged or resource-starved boards
Temporary overlays disappear when their decision ends

HUD and effects keep important actors and information visible

Single, multiple and all-target selections are immediately understandable
Every targetable enemy or part can be identified and selected
Approved final faces and art load instead of accidental placeholders
Art is judged as displayed in the game against a fixed target
Battle pose, facing, scale and contact fit the shot
A player's capability is demonstrated by that player's input
The evidence harness proves it captured the intended state
The deployed game is checked at the actual URL for its exact artifact
Shipping references resolve and remain stable
New generated or restored assets decode and contain intended content
Shared quality work is complete in both games
Every change belongs to the game or games it applies to
A win, loss or scene transition reaches its real destination
A subsystem is invoked through the real presentation path
Saves and settings survive an actual upgrade
A hidden experiment stays hidden and writes nothing to the save
A figure keeps its size, its height and its feet across a pose change
Motion is continuous: no snaps, double images, jerks at a swap or teleports (mid-move dashes reported)
Bailey judges audio beauty
Human feel assessment supplements measurements
Bailey's taste defines the approved target
